Behind the Broadcast: The Director's Cut

A downloadable game for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android

Download NowName your own price

You moved out — chasing your long-standing childhood dream of becoming a screenwriter.  Believing this little city is the perfect start for your fresh new career, you try your luck in the local movie studio where none other than the city's bombshell, Mr. Puzzles, seems rather impressed by your work. 

... Who? 

───────────────────────

Behind the Broadcast: The Director's Cut is a romance driven visual novel and a prequel to the Behind the Broadcast SMG4 AU. You do not need any knowledge of the SMG4 universe or my AU to play this! 

───────────────────────

THE GAME INCLUDES:

  • Gender neutral player (The game lets you pick your own name, but be aware that the text does include Elis' character features, such as jokes about her fur + her appearance in cutscenes)
  • 100+ Unique character sprites 
  • 6 Endings (3 major endings)
  • Around 35k words 
  • 11  fully animated cutscenes
  • Around 10 CGs
  • Pathetic TV man

───────────────────────

Available for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android !!

WARNING: some bad words, glitchy and shaky effects on text and cutscenes, unsettling ambience  (heartbeat, static) can trigger anxiety/discomfort 

CREDITS: 

Mr. Puzzles belongs to SMG4

Music/Sound Effects from: DOVA-SYNDROME, Freesound, MusMus, Pixabay

Hello world and folks! I'd like to dedicate this comment to the creator of this game; and if the creator is actually reading this I'd like to first let you know my sibling is a big fan of your game, but for whatever reason your app crashed on their android phone.

After some investigation using logcat and adb I realized that your Ren'Py bootstrap for the visual novel is outdated and still calls the os.makedirs directly on Android/data/ from this specific log:

09-26 20:07:41.409 I/python  (26973): Full traceback:

09-26 20:07:41.409 I/python  (26973):   File "renpy/bootstrap.py", line 399, in bootstrap

09-26 20:07:41.410 I/python  (26973):   File "<frozen os>", line 215, in makedirs

09-26 20:07:41.410 I/python  (26973):   File "<frozen os>", line 225, in makedirs

09-26 20:07:41.410 I/python  (26973): PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/storage/emulated/0/Android/data/com.elis.behindthebroadcast'

All I had to do though was just create a new folder in Android/data/ called com.elis.behindthebroadcast and another subfolder called files if anyone else is looking for a fix.

Thx in advance and on everything you do, I hope you publish an update to the android versions regarding this since it can be an issue on the newer, more locked down android versions with Scoped Storage since os.makedirs is blocked from creating the top-level app folder directly inside /Android/data/ among other directories. :/

I wish you well and cheers!
-ceqell

thatoneguy_ydf20 days ago(+2)

SPOILERS THIS WAY ⬇️
This visual novel is absolutely BEAUTIFUL. I really admire the slow romance aspect of it since I wasn't exactly fond of Mr P until we got to know him.

After figuring out his past with his parents and learning his opinion on love, I assumed the game was going to be a bit longer. When I found out he had been avoiding us, I immediately caught on that he was hiding his feelings by hiding himself, which was super funny and adorable! 

I also loved the reject ending; I got so scared Elis was ACTUALLY gonna mess with my files.

I must also admit I did have to Google a few of the endings because I am so good at romancing that I couldn't figure out any other way to end the game! The ending where we leave is by far the most heartbreaking, especially after falling for him. 

In all, I fell in love with Mr Puzzles; this VN brings out his character amazingly. The dialogue was well done, the characters are all lovable, the pacing is perfect, and all down to the last cc for our romance ending I was loving it.

PS: I'm a young writer myself, and I feel like I found this VN at just the right time. I have the biggest passion for writing, but I've felt so unmotivated recently... Elis's story gives me hope that my writing will too come alive one day as long as I keep going.

Thanks for the inspiration and new yumeship -Moxxie
